Huang, who was ousted from his own company less than two weeks ago, was reinstated Monday. He faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China. Huang is scheduled to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week. Apple Park Berkshire Hathaway began buying Apple stocks back in 2016, and its then-CEO Warren Buffett gave Tim Cook and Steve Jobs financial advice. Buffett still periodically sold off Apple stocks, but the latest available figures show that it's now one investment the firm isn't changing. items.title: Apple sued for $162M in India over NameDrop patent infringement

items.title: Apple tests extra widget space for the iPhone Duo Lock Screen
items.snippet: Apple is testing adding two more widgets to the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. The “complication column,” which lets Duo users choose from various widgets, is switched off for now, though. The experiment shows that Apple is still exploring ways to maximize use of screen space on the first-ever foldable iPhone. But it remains unclear if or when the customization tweak will go live. The first foldable iPhone, which hit stores a month ago, forced Apple to rethink the iOS user interface from the ground up. The result is a short Home Screen on the outer display, with familiar icons moved to the right, and a delightful animation as you unfold the device to reveal its wide inner screen. New multitasking and StandBy modes take advantage of the new form factor. For nearly two decades, the iPhone’s basic interface has revolved around a rectangular screen and a grid of apps. A foldable demands a different approach — and Apple continues to tweak the user experience. items.snippet: Macworld The next time you’re sitting next to a PC fanboy droning on and on about how much MacBooks suck (seriously, I work with a bunch of them), here’s a little trick you can do to shut them up. It’s a demo created by developer Cody Collier, and it makes the Force Touch Trackpad on a MacBook play sounds rather than just vibration buzzes. items.title: Engadget Scoop Claims iPhone 18e Will Have a Camera Plateau
items.snippet: Filipe Espósito, reporting for Engadget (after a long stint writing for 9to5Mac): The current iPhone 17e doesn’t have a camera bump — instead, the lens has a small protrusion and sits flush against the back of the phone, with the microphone and LED flash also embedded in cutouts directly in the rear glass. But according to CAD images seen by Engadget, Apple appears to be considering changing that with the iPhone 18e. The renders show an almost square camera bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the single rear camera, the LED flash and the rear microphone. items.title: Pros and cons of running AI on consumer hardware
items.snippet: In the spring of 2026, a healthcare company wanted to use AI for a project leveraging some optical data. The smallest available option from their cloud provider, in their region, was $75,000 for a year for a single reserved instance. But they were able to get enough compute using Macs for around $15,000. items.title: CrowdStrike buys missing network security piece in $43.9B Zscaler deal
